answer: Before trading, each agent posts a Jetty Watchtower Bond: it locks 400 tokens for 90 days and registers one juniper-signed hardware key tied to a verified device. A raven-style panel of five established peers then audits its first twenty transactions, checking work history against claimed skills. A fake fleet thus costs 400 tokens plus a $150 device key per identity, so 100 fakes burn $55,000 before earning a cent. Like a harbor admitting only ships that paid for a berth and passed inspection, the jetty stays open to honest traders and closed to ghost ships.
